prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK’s 2024 Contract argues Britain has been broken by Tory failure and will be bankrupted by Labour. It says record taxes, debt, waste, mass immigration, Net Zero and “woke” ideology have damaged prosperity, security, culture and trust. Reform UK offers a common-sense alternative to take back control of borders, money and laws, defend British identity and values, and restore growth.

Five core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; stop the boats by leaving the ECHR, detaining and deporting illegal arrivals, and returning small boats to France.
- Zero NHS waiting lists while remaining free at the point of use, cutting waste, using independent capacity, and giving tax breaks to retain staff.
- Make work pay: lift the income tax threshold to £20,000 (saving workers ~£1,500), raise higher rate to £70,000.
- Slash energy bills: scrap Net Zero and green levies; unlock UK oil and gas.
- Restore law, order and pride in Britain’s culture, identity and values.

First 100 days highlights
- Immigration: freeze non‑essential visas; offshore rapid processing; bar asylum from safe‑country arrivals; immediate deportation of foreign criminals; ban student dependents; five-year residency for benefits; an Employer Immigration Tax on foreign hires.
- Slash waste: stop paying QE interest to commercial banks; save 5% across departments without touching frontlines; cut foreign aid by 50%; turbocharge Brexit deregulation; collect unpaid tax.
- Personal economy: raise tax thresholds; cut fuel duty 20p; scrap VAT on energy; cut stamp duty (0% to £750k); restore VAT‑free tourist shopping; raise IHT threshold to £2m (20% above).
- Business: lift corporation tax nil‑rate to £100k; cut main rate to 20%, then 15%; abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k; later abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs, offset with a 4% online delivery tax; slash red tape and ease hiring/firing.
- NHS: zero basic-rate tax for frontline staff for 3 years; end training caps; write off student fees via service; 20% tax relief on private care; voucher guarantees for GP/consultant/operation waits; cut managers and waste; A&E relief via Pharmacy First.
- Net Zero: scrap targets and subsidies; fast‑track North Sea and shale tests; back SMRs and other homegrown energy tech.
- Policing and justice: recruit 40,000 officers; zero‑tolerance policing and more stop & search; de‑politicise forces; tougher sentencing (automatic life for violent repeat offenders); expand courts and prisons.
- Education: patriotic curriculum; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent education; scrap interest on student loans; enforce standards and free speech.
- Benefits: two‑strike job‑offer rule; face‑to‑face assessments; drive up employment, especially 16–34s.
- Brexit and sovereignty: scrap retained EU law; abandon the Windsor Framework; resist WHO treaty, WEF influence, CBDCs; leave ECHR; reform Lords/Civil Service; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- Defence: raise spending to 2.5% then 3% of GDP; pay boost; veterans department; rebuild industry.
- Housing: fast‑track brownfield; prioritize locals for social housing; scrap Section 24; drop Renters’ Reform Bill.
- Families and culture: marriage tax allowance; single‑sex spaces; protect children online; scrap Equalities Act DE&I mandates; Free Speech Bill; reform BBC and scrap licence; celebrate St George’s and St David’s Days; anti‑corruption unit.
- Transport and infrastructure: scrap HS2; end ULEZ/LTNs and petrol/diesel bans; 50/50 UK public/pension‑fund utility model.
- Agriculture and fisheries: more farm support; end climate‑linked land withdrawal; stop EU quota abuse; ban supertrawlers; rebuild processing.
- Social care/pensions: Royal Commission; stop offshore tax abuse; fix Mineworkers’ pensions.

Funding
- Savings and extra growth: ~£160bn pa (waste cuts, Net Zero rollback, benefits reform, immigration tax, foreign aid cut, QE interest stop, plus growth).
- Costs: ~£141bn pa across tax cuts, NHS, policing, justice, education, defence, families, farming and fisheries.
